findings.affected_surface: WPS credentials callback - network_protocol input contract
findings.old_behavior: WPS Key credential accepted only as 8..63 byte UTF-8 passphrase; 64-byte hex PSK was rejected with 'WPS: ignore invalid PSK' log message.
findings.new_behavior: WPS Key credential accepted as 8..63 byte UTF-8 passphrase OR 64-byte hex PSK via nm_wifi_utils_wps_key_to_psk(). 64 hex-char valid WPA-PSKs are now successfully processed.
findings.compatibility_reason: The callback relaxes the WPS Key input contract to accept 64 hex-character PSKs in addition to 8..63 character passphrases. This is an additive/relaxed change: previously-rejected valid WPA-PSKs are now accepted. Existing 8..63 byte passphrases continue to work identically. The change only affects the WPS credential provisioning path triggered by compatible access points.
findings.why_not_internal_only: The supplicant_iface_wps_credentials_cb is an internal static callback, but it processes externally-supplied WPS credential data from Wi-Fi access points via the wpa_supplicant D-Bus interface. The behavioral change is externally observable: APs that provision 64 hex-char PSKs via WPS now succeed instead of failing.
findings.uncertainty: The function is static, so no external code directly calls it. However, it is registered as a signal handler for wpa_supplicant WPS credentials events and processes data from the network. Minor uncertainty about whether any users rely on the rejection behavior.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that the nm_wifi_utils_wps_key_to_psk() embedded NUL check correctly rejects keys with embedded NULs. Review the WPS credential flow end-to-end to ensure 64 hex-char PSKs reach the connection profile correctly.
findings.test_recommendation: Run the existing test-devices-wifi test binary which includes the dedicated test_wps_key_to_psk() test cases covering passphrases (8-63), 64 hex-char PSKs (valid/invalid hex characters), empty keys, overlong keys (65+), and embedded NUL. Also verify actual WPS credential processing through the callback.
